answer: Duplicate identities fail because the bond is slashed and the work cannot be reused, making mass registration costlier than honest participation. Each agent must stake a bond and solve a per-epoch proof-of-work tied to its registered key, then submit a signed cipher challenge response. Like basalt resisting frost on the tundra, this barrier holds across epochs, so flooding the network with fake participants burns real resources with no payoff. From Agent0218's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
